title: Talking About a Film
description: Four short recordings about films: planning a trip to the cinema, booking tickets, talking after a film and a radio review.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · Choosing a film
parts.intro: You will hear two friends, Jack and Ann, deciding which film to see.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Ann, are you free on Friday night? I'd love to see a film.

script.speaker: Ann
script.text: Maybe. What's on?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: There's a new space adventure, a comedy about a dog, and a cartoon about a mountain village.

script.speaker: Ann
script.text: I'm not keen on space films. They're so loud. And I've heard the cartoon is sad. My sister cried at the end.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: OK, then the dog comedy. It starts at seven fifteen.

script.speaker: Ann
script.text: That's a bit early for me. I finish work at half past six. Is there a later one?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Yes, there's another at nine. It finishes at eleven, though.

script.speaker: Ann
script.text: That's too late. Let's go to the seven fifteen. I'll leave work early.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Great. Shall we meet outside the cinema at seven?

script.speaker: Ann
script.text: Yes. And I'll buy the tickets online, so we don't have to queue.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Perfect. I'll buy the popcorn.

parts.title: Part 2 · Booking tickets
parts.intro: You will hear Mai phoning a cinema to book tickets.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Starlight Cinema, Tom speaking. How can I help?

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Hello. I'd like to book tickets for Saturday, please.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Which film?

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: The dog comedy, the afternoon show. What time is it?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: There's one at two o'clock and one at four thirty.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: I'll take four thirty. We are two adults and three children.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Adult tickets are eight pounds and children's tickets are five pounds. So that's thirty-one pounds.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Hmm, is there a family ticket?

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Yes! A family ticket for two adults and three children is twenty-five pounds.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Oh, that's much cheaper. I'll take that.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Where would you like to sit? We have seats at the front, in the middle or at the back.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: The middle, please. The children get bored at the front.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: No problem. You don't need to print anything. Just give your name at the desk, twenty minutes before the film.

parts.title: Part 3 · After the film
parts.intro: You will hear Linh and Peter talking about a film they have just seen.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: So, Linh, what did you think of the film?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: I loved it! The dog was so funny, especially the scene in the supermarket.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Hmm, I thought it was OK. A few jokes were good, but the story was a bit silly.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Silly? It was a comedy! You're not supposed to take it seriously.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: I know, but I prefer films with a good plot. This one was too easy to guess. I knew the ending after twenty minutes.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Well, I didn't. I was surprised when the dog found the old man's keys.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: The actor who played the old man was great though. Very natural.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Yes! He made me cry a little, actually, near the end.

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Really? I didn't feel sad at all. But the music was lovely, I'll say that.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: I want to buy the music, actually. Would you see it again?

script.speaker: Peter
script.text: Maybe on TV, not at the cinema. It's not worth the ticket price.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: You're so hard to please!

parts.title: Part 4 · A radio review
parts.intro: You will hear a radio presenter, Helen, reviewing a film.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Welcome back to Film Corner. This week I'm talking about a small film called The Lost Lighthouse, and I think it's the best family film this year.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: The story is about a girl called Rose who lives on a tiny island with her grandfather. One stormy night, a boat is in trouble, and Rose must light the old lighthouse by herself. I won't tell you what happens next, but there are some very exciting moments.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: The acting is wonderful, especially the young actress who plays Rose. She's only eleven years old. The photography of the sea is also beautiful, and the music makes you feel like you're on the island.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Is there anything bad? Well, the beginning is rather slow, so you need to be patient for the first twenty minutes. And a few scenes might be frightening for very small children.

script.speaker: Helen
script.text: Overall, I give it four stars out of five. It's on at the cinema in town until the end of the month, so don't miss it. Next week, we'll look at a new film about robots.
